Roofing and Spray Foam Surveys

A specialist roofing and spray foam survey takes 1 to 2 hours on site, with photos and clear recommendations at the end. Call us to arrange a professional survey.

What We Check

The roof structure, the condition of the timbers, moisture levels, ventilation, the roofing felt and any existing spray foam. You get photographs, moisture readings where they are needed, and clear recommendations for any work that is needed.

Only What Needs Doing

We don't automatically recommend expensive removal or replacement. We tell you what genuinely needs attention and what may not need any work at all. As roofers and spray foam removal specialists we understand the whole roof, which helps when you need to answer questions from a surveyor or a mortgage lender.

What Others Get Wrong

We see homeowners advised to spend thousands of pounds they didn't need to, because the contractor didn't know enough to look at other options. We've met people quoted £20,000 for a new roof when the spray foam could have been removed for much less.

A Recent Job

A homeowner in the Midlands had been told by several roofers that the closed-cell spray foam meant a whole new roof, at about £20,000. Our two-hour inspection found the foam could be removed carefully by hand, with no new roof and no abrasive ice blasting, which can damage roofing materials. Our team removed it for £8,000, saving the customer about £12,000, and the work was fully documented, signed off and certificated.

When to Book a Survey

  • You have roofing defects or leaks
  • You're worried about spray foam in the loft
  • You are having trouble with a mortgage because of the roof or the foam
  • A surveyor's report has flagged a problem with the roof

How Long It Takes

A specialist survey usually takes 1 to 2 hours on site.

What the Government Says

The government published guidance on spray foam, mortgages and removal on 22 October 2026. It says to get advice from a specialist surveyor before deciding, and that removal won't always mean a lender will lend. Read our summary of the guidance.
